headline: 63-run loss: Bangladesh miss out on Bronze at Asian Games
summary: The Tigers suffer a crushing defeat to a second-string Sri Lankan side, returning home empty-handed for the first time in the tournament's history.
details: Bangladesh suffered a 63-run defeat to a second-string Sri Lanka side in the third-place playoff at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan.
The Litton Das-led team was bowled out for 102 in 17.3 overs, failing to reach the target of 166.
Sri Lanka posted a competitive total of 165 for nine in their 20 overs, supported by Tharindu Ratnayake's 32 off 25 deliveries.
The Tigers' batting collapse was severe, losing four wickets for just 18 runs in the first 3.5 overs of the chase.
Top-order batters Saif Hassan, Tanzid Tamim, and skipper Litton Das all failed to score a single run.
Nasum Ahmed top-scored for Bangladesh with 26 off 28 balls, while Parvez Hossain Emon and Yasir Ali contributed 20 and 21 runs respectively.
For Sri Lanka, Nuwan Thushara, Tharindu Ratnayake, Tharindu Viyaskanth and Wanuja Sahan each took two wickets.
This loss means Bangladesh returns home without a medal, marking the first time they have failed to secure a medal at the Asian Games.
caption:
Empty-handed for the first time. Bangladesh loses the Bronze medal match to a second-string Sri Lankan side.

Bangladesh suffered a 63-run defeat to a second-string Sri Lanka side in the third-place playoff at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan.

The Litton Das-led team was bowled out for 102 in 17.3 overs, failing to reach the target of 166.

Sri Lanka posted a competitive total of 165 for nine in their 20 overs, supported by Tharindu Ratnayake's 32 off 25 deliveries.

The Tigers' batting collapse was severe, losing four wickets for just 18 runs in the first 3.5 overs of the chase.

Top-order batters Saif Hassan, Tanzid Tamim, and skipper Litton Das all failed to score a single run.

Nasum Ahmed top-scored for Bangladesh with 26 off 28 balls, while Parvez Hossain Emon and Yasir Ali contributed 20 and 21 runs respectively.

For Sri Lanka, Nuwan Thushara, Tharindu Ratnayake, Tharindu Viyaskanth and Wanuja Sahan each took two wickets.

This loss means Bangladesh returns home without a medal, marking the first time they have failed to secure a medal at the Asian Games.
